title: DO_SIGN/VERIFY/AGREE: ioctl_do_sign uses fget to prevent teardown during sign — verified correct
description: Race analysis: Thread A calls close() on a KEY fd while Thread B calls DO_SIGN with key_fd pointing to the same KEY fd. fget(op.key_fd) in Thread B increments the file refcount. The close() in Thread A decrements the refcount but does not call release() until refcount hits zero. So Thread B's fget holds the file alive. Thread B then takes key_state->lock. Thread A's close path (crypto2dev_fd_release) also takes state->lock. Since Thread B holds the lock, Thread A blocks. Thread B completes the sign operation, drops the lock, calls fput() (which decrements refcount). Only now does Thread A's close proceed. This ordering is safe: no use-after-free. The fget/fput protocol correctly prevents the KEY fd from being torn down while DO_SIGN is using it. Verified correct — no race. Closing.
